items.question: Many bacteria and protozoa split into two equal halves to reproduce. What is this called?
items.explanation: Splitting one cell into two is binary fission; splitting into many at once is multiple fission.

items.question: Which of these is a method of vegetative propagation used by farmers?
items.explanation: Layering and grafting grow new plants from plant parts, as with sugarcane, roses or grapes.

items.question: Which part of a flower is the male reproductive part that produces pollen grains?
items.explanation: The stamen makes the yellowish pollen; the pistil in the centre is the female part.

items.question: Where are sperms formed in the human male?
items.explanation: The testes form the sperms; the prostate and seminal vesicles only add fluid.

items.question: Which method of avoiding pregnancy also helps prevent the spread of many sexually transmitted infections?
options: Surgical blocking of the fallopian tubes
items.explanation: A condom is a physical barrier, so it also reduces the passing on of many infections; the others do not.

items.question: Why are the two cells formed by cell division similar but not always identical?
options: Each cell receives DNA from two parents
The reactions that copy DNA are never absolutely accurate
The environment rewrites their DNA every time
One of the cells receives no DNA
items.explanation: Small errors in copying DNA mean the copies can differ slightly from the original.

items.question: How does Hydra reproduce by budding?
options: It splits into two equal halves
An outgrowth forms by repeated cell division at one spot, then detaches as a new individual
Its body breaks into many fragments
items.explanation: The bud grows into a tiny Hydra on the parent and separates when it is mature.

items.question: In bread mould (Rhizopus), which structures hold the spores?
items.explanation: The tiny blob-on-a-stick structures are sporangia; the threads are hyphae, which do not reproduce.

items.question: How does sexual reproduction speed up the creation of variation?
options: It combines DNA from two different individuals, making new combinations of variants
It makes DNA copying much less accurate
It copies the DNA of one parent exactly
It removes all the variations that exist
items.explanation: Each parent carries different accumulated variations, so mixing them produces new combinations.

items.question: What happens to the thickened lining of the uterus if the egg is not fertilised?
options: It slowly breaks down and leaves the body as blood and mucus
items.explanation: The lining is no longer needed, so it is shed; this is menstruation.

items.question: How is binary fission in Leishmania different from binary fission in Amoeba?
options: Leishmania divides into many cells at once
Amoeba can split only along one plane
Leishmania splits in a definite orientation relative to its whip-like structure; Amoeba can split in any plane
items.explanation: Leishmania has a whip-like structure at one end, and its division is lined up with it.

items.question: A grower wants new rose plants that keep every feature of a prized parent plant and flower sooner. Which method fits best, and why?
options: Growing from seed, because seeds always give identical plants
Cross-pollination, because it creates new varieties
Spore formation, because roses make spores
Vegetative propagation, because the new plants are genetically similar to the parent and flower earlier
items.explanation: Plants from vegetative propagation keep the parent's characteristics and bear flowers earlier than seedlings.

items.question: After fertilisation in a flower, what do the ovule and the ovary become?
options: The ovule becomes a seed and the ovary ripens into a fruit
The ovule becomes a fruit and the ovary becomes a seed
items.explanation: The ovule, with the embryo inside, develops a tough coat and becomes the seed; the ovary grows into the fruit.

items.question: What is the role of the placenta?
options: It lets glucose and oxygen pass from the mother's blood to the embryo, and wastes pass back
It releases an egg every month
items.explanation: The placenta's villi give a large surface where materials pass between the mother's blood and the embryo.

items.question: How do oral contraceptive pills prevent pregnancy?
options: They change the body's hormonal balance so that eggs are not released
They are placed in the uterus
items.explanation: Pills act on hormones, so no egg is released; because of this they can also have side-effects.
